citation.title: GANTL: Towards Practical and Real-Time Topology Optimization with Conditional GANs and Transfer Learning
citation.authors: Mohammad Mahdi Behzadi; Horea T. Ilies

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Across the first reported testing scenario, GANTL predictions average 1.00% compliance-map error relative to SIMP reference designs.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Introduction cites 1.85 s per SIMP iteration, but gives no corresponding GANTL time; no ratio can be derived.
claim.alternatives: Abstract and conclusion emphasize smaller training sets and better connectivity relative to other learned methods; introduction calls classical TO computationally costly but gives no paired ML timing.

baseline.hardware_classical: UConn HPC facility running Red Hat RHEL7; CPU details not stated (section 3.5)
baseline.hardware_ml: UConn HPC facility running Red Hat RHEL7; processor details not stated (section 3.5)
baseline.classical_time: 1.85 s per iteration for a 300 x 100 MMB beam, cited from reference 4 (introduction); no own benchmark time stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; section 5 refers to a different paper for discussion
baseline.quality_metric: Pixelwise compliance-map error, image MSE, binary accuracy (section 3.5; Tables 2-5)
baseline.quality_gap: Table 2: average compliance-map error 1.00% for seen boundary conditions with one force; Table 3 and Table 4 report larger errors for unseen conditions or additional forces

R1.evidence: Section 4.2/Table 2: primary quantitative comparison concerns compliance-map error, without paired runtime comparison.

R2.evidence: Section 4.2/Table 2: primary quantitative comparison concerns compliance-map error, without paired runtime comparison.

R3.evidence: Section 4.2/Table 2: primary quantitative comparison concerns compliance-map error, without paired runtime comparison.

R4.evidence: Section 3.5 defines compliance error as a pixelwise difference of predicted and reference compliance maps; Tables 2-5 also use MSE and binary accuracy. No FE analysis of every returned design, volume-violation tally, or failure-rate tally is reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Table 2: 7,473 at 40 x 80, 350 at 80 x 160, 463 at 120 x 160, 388 at 120 x 240, 350 at 160 x 320, and 350 at 200 x 400; further cases in Tables 3-5

notes: Section 4.2 compares design-image and compliance-map measures with SIMP. The introduction gives a cited classical per-iteration time, but the paper gives no matched GANTL inference time. The abstract's data-efficiency claim compares with other learned methods. Section 3.4 states a 0.5 volume fraction and 1.5 filter radius for the SIMP reference designs, but does not establish returned-design feasibility.
